reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown read Acts 1:15's 120 as only the Jerusalem remnant, since many of the 500 believers Paul mentions likely stayed behind in Galilee.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg says Acts counts only 120 brethren, ignored by Paul's separate report of five hundred witnesses at once.

quotes.text: He says Jesus was seen by five hundred brethren at once. The Evangelists are all ignorant of this appearance, while the author of Acts states that there were but one hundred and twenty “brethren” in all
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), ch. XX, on Acts 1:15 and 1 Corinthians 15:6.

sides.verseText: In these days, Peter stood up in the midst of the disciples (and the number of names was about one hundred twenty), and said,

sides.snippet: over five hundred brothers at once
sides.verseText: Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.
